title: Detecting Contextual Hallucinations Using Only Attention Maps
one_line_claim: Detects contextual hallucinations via attention-based lookback ratio features computed from transformer attention maps, enabling cross-model transfer without retraining.
method_summary: Extracts the ratio of attention weights on context tokens versus newly generated tokens for each head and layer, averaging these lookback ratios across heads and layers into a feature vector. Trains a logistic regression classifier on this vector to predict hallucination probability for token spans, applied during decoding to guide generation.

key_findings.finding: Lookback Lens achieves slightly better performance than hidden-states-based classifiers and significantly outperforms NLI baselines on the predefined span task.
key_findings.quote: the Lookback Lens achieves slightly better performance than the hidden states-based classifier and significantly outperforms the NLI models (SoTA and our impl.).

key_findings.finding: Lookback Lens Guided Decoding reduces hallucinations by 9.6% in XSum summarization compared to greedy decoding.
key_findings.quote: a simple classifier-guided decoding approach is able to reduce the amount of hallucination, for example by 9.6% in the XSum summarization task

key_findings.finding: Detectors trained on a 7B model transfer to larger 13B models without retraining.
key_findings.quote: the Lookback Lens is found to transfer across tasks and even models, allowing a detector that is trained on a 7B model to be applied (without retraining) to a larger 13B model

relation_to_herald.shared: Both detect quality degradation using runtime token-level signals during generation; both use lightweight classifiers trained on per-token features rather than hidden states; both are applied during decoding for real-time intervention.
differs_on: Lookback Lens detects contextual hallucinations (contradictions with provided context) via attention map ratios; HERALD predicts compression-induced catastrophic failures (looping, non-termination) via logit-based time-series features.
Lookback Lens uses attention weights as the sole signal; HERALD uses log-probability sequences from the logit distribution.
Lookback Lens operates on summarization/QA tasks with pre-allocated context; HERALD targets long-context scenarios where KV-cache compression induces failures.
